articles.title: Indian tech company eMudhra announces withdrawal from certificate business after security
articles.summary: Because of the weak keys, any attacker could create a forged certificate for any domain and use it to impersonate servers to intercept or modify traffic. The issue was publicized by cybersecurity researcher Scott Helme, who published a blog saying that instead of a random 384-bit number, one of the private keys was just the number four.

articles.title: UN biodiversity summit to take stock of 2030 goals
articles.summary: Representatives from 196 countries are meeting in Yerevan to evaluate biodiversity progress under the 2030 targets. The Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework aims to restore ecosystems and phase out harmful subsidies. India's national report highlights progress with key wildlife species, despite challenges in land degradation and protected areas. The report shows India's successful ecosystem restoration and involvement in biodiversity-inclusive planning.

articles.title: Diljit Dosanjh's Delhi concert denied permission by police over security concerns
articles.summary: Singer Diljit Dosanjh’s concert, scheduled to take place at Delhi’s Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium on October 30, has been denied permission by the Delhi Police, citing security concerns. The decision comes as a setback for fans who had been looking forward to attending the live concert. Further details about the event and ticket-related arrangements are awaited.

articles.title: Indians racially abused, threatened in Australia: 19-year-old threatens to blow up Indian
articles.summary: Indians Threatened in Australia: An incident of racial hate crime has come to light in Australia, where a 19-year-old Australian man has been arrested after he allegedly made racially abusive remarks to an Indian family in Brisbane. He also threatened to ‘blow up’ the Indian family’s apartment building on Monday.

articles.title: PM Modi-Tusk talks: India and Poland push for defence, space and trade ties
articles.summary: For Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk, the answer stretches from defence equipment and space technology to trade, energy and a shared approach to global affairs.
